rules.title: Contract Price & Payment Terms
rules.employer_focus: Verify payment schedule, milestone triggers, and interim payment certificate timelines are clearly defined and enforceable.
rules.contractor_focus: Verify your right to interim payments, payment certificate timelines, and consequences of late payment including financing charges.
compliance_indicators: Payment schedule defined with milestone triggers
Late payment interest or remedy stated
Currency and exchange rate provisions present
red_flags_employer: Payment triggered by subjective Employer satisfaction rather than objective milestones
No Engineer obligation to issue certificates within defined period
Currency provisions absent in cross-border contracts
red_flags_contractor: Payment period exceeds 56 days from Engineer certificate
No financing charges for late payment
Employer right to withhold payment without Engineer certification
rules.corrective_language: The Engineer shall issue an Interim Payment Certificate within 28 days of receiving a Statement. The Employer shall pay within 56 days of the Engineer receiving the Statement. If payment is delayed, financing charges at the rate of [LIBOR/SOFR + 3%] per annum shall apply.
rules.financial_exposure: Late or withheld payment on GCC mega-projects can create cash flow crises. Contractor financing costs on delayed payments of USD 10M at 8% per annum equal USD 800,000 annually.

rules.title: Contractor Rights to Suspend Works
rules.employer_focus: Ensure suspension rights are conditional on proper notice and defined non-payment thresholds to prevent frivolous suspension claims.
rules.contractor_focus: Verify your right to suspend is clearly preserved after 21 days of non-payment following notice, with cost and time entitlement on resumption.
compliance_indicators: Contractor entitlement to costs on suspension confirmed
Contractor entitlement to EOT on suspension confirmed
Contractor termination right after prolonged suspension stated
red_flags_employer: Suspension rights removed entirely
Notice period extended beyond 21 days without compensation
No defined resumption obligation
red_flags_contractor: Suspension right conditional on Employer consent
No cost entitlement on valid suspension
No termination right after 84 days of suspension
rules.corrective_language: If the Employer fails to comply with Clause 14.7, the Contractor may, after giving not less than 21 days notice to the Employer, suspend work or reduce the rate of work. The Contractor shall be entitled to an extension of time and additional costs incurred by reason of such suspension.
rules.financial_exposure: Removal of suspension rights eliminates a critical contractor lever. Continued mobilisation without payment on a USD 50M contract can generate USD 500,000 to USD 1.5M monthly cash burn.

rules.title: Extension of Time for Completion
rules.employer_focus: Ensure EOT triggers are limited to defined events only. Verify notification windows are enforceable. Confirm Engineer has structured response obligation.
rules.contractor_focus: Verify all standard EOT trigger events are preserved. Confirm 28-day notification window. Verify Engineer cannot unreasonably withhold EOT determination.
compliance_indicators: EOT trigger events listed and comprehensive
Engineer response obligation and timeline defined
Exceptional adverse weather defined and included
red_flags_employer: Notification window reduced below 28 days
EOT trigger events narrowed removing legitimate Employer-risk events
No Engineer response deadline allowing indefinite delay of determination
Force majeure excluded from EOT triggers
red_flags_contractor: Notification window reduced to 7 days or less
Concurrent delay clause eliminates all contractor EOT entitlement
Employer-caused delays excluded from EOT triggers
Time at large risk not addressed
rules.corrective_language: The Contractor shall be entitled to an extension of time if completion is or will be delayed by: (a) a Variation; (b) a cause of delay giving entitlement under a Sub-Clause of these Conditions; (c) exceptionally adverse climatic conditions; (d) Unforeseeable shortages; or (e) any delay caused by the Employer or Engineer. Notice shall be given within 28 days of awareness. The Engineer shall respond within 42 days.
rules.financial_exposure: A 7-day notification window on a complex GCC project makes time bar almost inevitable on Employer-caused delays. If time at large is argued successfully in ICC arbitration, liquidated damages become unenforceable. On a USD 100M project with USD 100,000 per day LD, this represents an uncapped exposure.

rules.title: Variation Orders & Valuation
rules.employer_focus: Ensure variation instruction rights are preserved without contractor veto. Verify valuation methodology is objective and Engineer-led.
rules.contractor_focus: Verify right to object to variations that cannot be executed. Confirm valuation methodology includes overhead and profit. Verify omission-to-benefit-third-party restriction.
compliance_indicators: Employer right to instruct variations confirmed
Contractor right to object on reasonable grounds preserved
Prohibition on omission to give work to third party stated
red_flags_employer: Contractor veto on variations without qualification
Valuation methodology absent allowing disputes
No dayworks schedule included
red_flags_contractor: Overhead and profit excluded from variation valuation
No right to object to impossible variations
Omissions can be reassigned to third parties
rules.corrective_language: The Engineer may instruct Variations at any time prior to issuing the Taking-Over Certificate. The Contractor shall not omit any work except by a Variation instruction. Each Variation shall be valued at the rates in the Contract, or if not applicable, at rates agreed or determined by the Engineer including reasonable overhead and profit.
rules.financial_exposure: Variation valuation disputes are the most common source of GCC construction arbitration. Absence of a clear valuation methodology can result in disputed claims representing 10-20% of contract value.

rules.title: Termination by Employer
rules.employer_focus: Verify defined grounds for termination exist, notice-to-correct periods are preserved, and post-termination cost recovery mechanisms are clear.
rules.contractor_focus: Verify termination grounds are specific and not open-ended. Confirm 14-day notice-to-correct period. Verify payment on termination includes work done and plant on site.
red_flags_employer: Termination clause absent entirely
Termination grounds vague or undefined
No cost recovery mechanism post termination
red_flags_contractor: Termination for convenience without fair payment
No notice-to-correct period before termination
Post-termination payment excludes loss of profit
rules.corrective_language: The Employer shall be entitled to terminate the Contract if the Contractor: (a) fails to comply with a notice to correct within 14 days; (b) abandons the Works; (c) becomes insolvent; (d) gives or offers a bribe. On termination, the Employer may complete the Works and recover excess costs from the Contractor after accounting for amounts due.
rules.financial_exposure: Absence of a termination clause means any termination issued becomes wrongful termination by default. A wrongful termination claim on a USD 50M contract typically includes loss of profit on remaining works (10-15%) plus demobilisation costs, potentially USD 7-10M in exposure.

rules.title: Termination by Contractor
rules.employer_focus: Verify contractor termination rights are limited to defined grounds with proper notice requirements to prevent opportunistic termination.
rules.contractor_focus: Verify your right to terminate for sustained non-payment, prolonged suspension, or Employer insolvency, with full payment including loss of profit.
compliance_indicators: Payment on termination includes profit on unexecuted works
Prolonged suspension as termination ground included
Employer insolvency as termination ground included
red_flags_employer: Contractor termination grounds overly broad
No notice period requirement before contractor termination
Loss of profit payable on termination for convenience
red_flags_contractor: Contractor termination rights removed
Non-payment not listed as termination ground
No loss of profit payable on valid termination
rules.corrective_language: The Contractor may terminate the Contract if the Employer fails to pay amounts due within 42 days after the expiry of the payment period, or if the Works are suspended for more than 84 days. On termination, the Employer shall pay the Contract Price attributable to work executed plus reasonable profit on unexecuted work.
rules.financial_exposure: Removal of contractor termination rights traps the contractor in a non-performing contract. Continued mobilisation against a non-paying employer can generate monthly losses of 2-5% of monthly contract value with no exit mechanism.

rules.title: Contractor Claims Notification & Time Bar
rules.employer_focus: Ensure time bar is clearly defined with specific trigger date, consequences of late notification stated, and ongoing events addressed.
rules.contractor_focus: Verify 28-day notification window from awareness not event. Confirm ongoing events clause. Verify time bar consequence does not eliminate underlying entitlement for Employer-caused events.
red_flags_employer: Clock start date undefined allowing open-ended claims
No time bar consequence stated
Ongoing events not addressed allowing accumulating claims
red_flags_contractor: Notification window reduced below 28 days
Time bar eliminates entitlement for Employer-caused events
No ongoing events provision
Awareness standard replaced with event date only
rules.corrective_language: The Contractor shall give notice to the Engineer as soon as practicable and not later than 28 days after the Contractor became aware, or should have become aware, of the event. If the Contractor fails to give notice within 28 days, the Time for Completion shall not be extended and the Contractor shall not be entitled to additional payment. For continuing events, monthly notices shall be submitted.
rules.financial_exposure: An ambiguous time bar in ICC arbitration is routinely interpreted in favour of the claimant. Without a clear clock start date, the time bar provides no protection. Unmanaged claims on GCC infrastructure projects have historically reached 15-25% of contract value.

rules.title: Dispute Avoidance and Adjudication Board
rules.employer_focus: Verify DAAB appointment timeline, decision binding nature, and failure to comply with DAAB decision as grounds for immediate arbitration.
rules.contractor_focus: Verify DAAB is mandatory not optional, appointment is joint not unilateral, and decisions are immediately binding pending arbitration.
red_flags_employer: DAAB made optional, removing mandatory first tier
Employer unilateral right to appoint DAAB members
Arbitration clause designates inconvenient seat
red_flags_contractor: DAAB removed entirely collapsing to direct arbitration
DAAB decisions not binding pending arbitration
Notice of dissatisfaction period shortened below 28 days
rules.corrective_language: The Parties shall jointly appoint a DAAB within 28 days of the Commencement Date. The DAAB shall visit the Site regularly. DAAB decisions shall be binding on both Parties who shall promptly comply pending arbitration. A Party may give Notice of Dissatisfaction within 28 days of receiving a decision.
rules.financial_exposure: Removal of DAAB collapses dispute resolution to direct arbitration. ICC arbitration on a USD 20M dispute typically costs USD 1-3M in fees and takes 2-4 years. DAAB resolution costs a fraction and resolves in weeks.

rules.title: Insurance Requirements
rules.employer_focus: Verify required insurances are listed with minimum coverage amounts, Employer named as additional insured, and evidence of insurance required before commencement.
rules.contractor_focus: Verify insurance requirements are commercially achievable, coverage amounts are proportionate to contract value, and Employer cannot unilaterally change requirements.
compliance_indicators: Evidence of insurance before commencement required
red_flags_employer: No minimum coverage amounts stated
Employer not named as additional insured
No requirement to provide evidence before commencement
red_flags_contractor: Coverage amounts disproportionate to contract value
Employer right to unilaterally increase coverage requirements
No cross liability waiver
rules.corrective_language: Before the Commencement Date, the Contractor shall effect and maintain insurances including: (a) Works insurance for full replacement value; (b) Third party liability of not less than [USD amount]; (c) Employer's liability and workers' compensation as required by law. The Employer shall be named as additional insured on all policies.
rules.financial_exposure: Inadequate insurance on a GCC construction project can leave uninsured losses of tens of millions. A fire or collapse event without adequate works insurance creates direct loss to whichever party bears the risk under the contract.

rules.title: Defects Liability Period & Notification
rules.employer_focus: Verify DLP duration is appropriate, Employer right to notify defects is clearly preserved, and contractor obligation to remedy within defined period is stated.
rules.contractor_focus: Verify DLP duration is not excessive, latent defect liability is time-limited, and Performance Certificate issued promptly after DLP expiry.
compliance_indicators: Contractor remedy obligation and timeline stated
red_flags_employer: DLP extended beyond 24 months without justification
No contractor remedy timeline creating open-ended obligation
Performance Certificate withheld without reason
red_flags_contractor: DLP duration unlimited or undefined
No Performance Certificate mechanism releasing contractor
Latent defect liability extends beyond reasonable period
rules.corrective_language: The Contractor shall complete outstanding work and remedy defects notified during the Defects Notification Period of [365] days. The Engineer shall issue the Performance Certificate within 28 days of expiry of the DLP confirming that the Contractor has completed all obligations. The Performance Certificate constitutes the only approval of the Works.
rules.financial_exposure: An undefined DLP exposes the contractor to perpetual liability. Retention held against an open DLP on a USD 20M contract at 5% retention equals USD 1M held indefinitely.

rules.title: Force Majeure & Exceptional Events
rules.employer_focus: Verify force majeure definition is not overly broad, notification requirements are clear, and prolonged force majeure termination rights are balanced.
rules.contractor_focus: Verify force majeure includes natural disasters, war, and government actions. Confirm EOT entitlement. Verify cost entitlement for specific events.
compliance_indicators: EOT entitlement on force majeure confirmed
Cost entitlement for specific events stated
Prolonged force majeure termination right included
red_flags_employer: Force majeure definition so broad it covers normal commercial risk
No notification requirement allowing retrospective claims
No cap on force majeure cost entitlement
red_flags_contractor: Force majeure excludes government actions relevant to GCC projects
No cost entitlement even for Employer-risk force majeure events
Prolonged force majeure termination right removed
rules.corrective_language: Force Majeure means an exceptional event beyond a Party's control that was unforeseeable, unavoidable, and not substantially attributable to the other Party. The affected Party shall give notice within 14 days. The Contractor shall be entitled to an extension of time and, for events listed in Sub-Clause 19.4, additional cost.
rules.financial_exposure: GCC projects face specific force majeure risks including government policy changes, regional conflict, and pandemic-level disruptions. Without adequate force majeure provisions, contractors absorb costs that should be Employer-risk events.

rules.title: Engineer Authority & Impartiality
rules.employer_focus: Ensure Engineer authority is clearly defined, determination process is structured, and Engineer acts as contract administrator not Employer agent.
rules.contractor_focus: Verify Engineer has genuine determination authority independent of Employer instruction. Confirm Engineer response deadlines. Verify Engineer cannot override FIDIC entitlements.
compliance_indicators: Response timelines for Engineer decisions stated
Employer right to replace Engineer with notice stated
red_flags_employer: Engineer acts as pure Employer agent with no independent role
No structured determination process
Engineer replacement without notice to Contractor
red_flags_contractor: Engineer determination subject to Employer approval
No Engineer response deadlines
Engineer authority to override FIDIC entitlements
rules.corrective_language: The Engineer shall act as a skilled professional. When making determinations under Clause 3.5, the Engineer shall consult with each Party and make a fair determination in accordance with the Contract. The Engineer shall respond to Contractor submissions within 28 days unless a longer period is agreed.
rules.financial_exposure: An Engineer acting purely as Employer agent eliminates the administrative balance of the FIDIC framework. All determinations become potentially biased, driving every dispute to DAAB or arbitration with associated costs.

rules.title: Taking Over Certificate & Completion
rules.employer_focus: Verify Taking Over Certificate triggers end of Contractor risk for the Works. Confirm Employer cannot unreasonably withhold issuance.
rules.contractor_focus: Verify Taking Over Certificate triggers end of insurance obligations, transfers care of Works to Employer, and stops LD accrual.
compliance_indicators: Taking Over Certificate issuance obligation stated
Engineer response deadline to Taking Over application defined
Risk transfer on Taking Over confirmed
LD cessation on Taking Over stated
red_flags_employer: No obligation to issue Taking Over Certificate
Taking Over subject to subjective Employer satisfaction
LDs continue to accrue after practical completion
red_flags_contractor: Taking Over Certificate withheld for minor defects
No partial Taking Over for completed sections
No deemed Taking Over after prolonged Engineer inaction
rules.corrective_language: The Engineer shall issue the Taking-Over Certificate within 28 days after receiving the Contractor's application if the Works are substantially complete. If the Engineer fails to act within 28 days, the Taking-Over Certificate shall be deemed to have been issued on the date the Works were substantially complete.
rules.financial_exposure: Delayed Taking Over Certificate means LDs continue to accrue on a completed project. On a USD 100M project with USD 150,000 per day LDs, a 30-day delay in issuing the certificate equals USD 4.5M of unwarranted LD exposure.

rules.title: Interim Payment Certificates & Retention
rules.employer_focus: Verify interim payment process is clear, retention percentage and release mechanism are defined, and Engineer certification obligation is stated.
rules.contractor_focus: Verify retention percentage does not exceed 5%, first half release on Taking Over is automatic, and second half release on Performance Certificate is stated.
red_flags_employer: Retention percentage exceeds 10%
Retention release subject to Employer discretion not Engineer certificate
No Engineer certification timeline
red_flags_contractor: Retention exceeds 5% of contract value
Retention release tied to conditions beyond DLP expiry
No mechanism for retention bond in lieu of cash retention
rules.corrective_language: The Employer shall retain [5%] of each interim payment up to a maximum of [5%] of the Contract Price. One half of the retention shall be certified for payment in the Taking-Over Certificate. The remainder shall be certified in the Performance Certificate. The Contractor may substitute a retention bond for cash retention.
rules.financial_exposure: Retention held at 10% instead of 5% on a USD 50M contract equals USD 2.5M additional cash withheld. Over a 24-month DLP, the financing cost to the contractor at 8% per annum equals USD 200,000 of pure financing cost on excess retention.

rules.title: Subcontracting Obligations
rules.employer_focus: Verify Contractor remains fully responsible for all Subcontractor performance. Confirm approval process for Subcontractors is defined.
rules.contractor_focus: Verify Subcontractor approval cannot be unreasonably withheld. Confirm Employer-nominated Subcontractors carry appropriate risk transfer.
compliance_indicators: Contractor liability for Subcontractor acts confirmed
Domestic Subcontractor list provisions included if applicable
red_flags_employer: Contractor not fully liable for Subcontractor performance
No approval process for critical Subcontractors
red_flags_contractor: Employer can withhold Subcontractor approval unreasonably
Nominated Subcontractors carry risk that should transfer to Employer
rules.corrective_language: The Contractor shall not subcontract the whole of the Works. The Contractor shall be responsible for all Subcontractors acts and omissions as if they were the acts of the Contractor. The Contractor shall not subcontract any part of the Works without the prior consent of the Engineer, which shall not be unreasonably withheld.
rules.financial_exposure: Inadequate subcontracting provisions create gaps in liability chains. If a Subcontractor defaults and the Contractor is not clearly liable, the Employer bears uninsured losses for delayed or defective work.

rules.title: Programme & Progress Reporting
rules.employer_focus: Verify programme submission timeline, Engineer review and consent obligations, and consequences of programme non-submission are defined.
rules.contractor_focus: Verify programme consent cannot be unreasonably withheld and programme revision rights are preserved following change events.
compliance_indicators: Revised programme obligations on change events stated
red_flags_employer: No consequence for failure to submit programme
Engineer programme consent with no timeline creating indefinite review
red_flags_contractor: Programme consent treated as approval of method preventing claims
No right to revise programme after change events
rules.corrective_language: The Contractor shall submit a detailed programme within 28 days of the Commencement Date. The programme shall show the order and timing of all activities. The Engineer shall review and respond within 21 days. If the Engineer raises no objection, the programme shall be accepted. The Contractor shall revise the programme on any event causing delay.
rules.financial_exposure: Absence of an agreed programme eliminates the baseline for delay analysis. Without a programme baseline, EOT claims cannot be properly quantified and are routinely rejected or undervalued.

rules.title: Liquidated Damages for Delay
rules.employer_focus: Verify LD rate is stated, cap on LDs is defined, and LD clause does not prevent termination for prolonged delay.
rules.contractor_focus: Verify LD rate is the Employer's sole remedy for delay, LD cap is reasonable, and LDs cease on Taking Over.
compliance_indicators: LD rate per day clearly stated
LD cap as percentage of Contract Price defined
LDs as sole remedy for delay confirmed
LD cessation on Taking Over stated
red_flags_employer: No LD cap exposing Contractor to unlimited liability
LD rate not stated leaving damages at large
LDs do not constitute sole remedy for delay
red_flags_contractor: No LD cap or cap exceeds 20% of contract value
LDs continue to accrue after Taking Over
General damages reserved in addition to LDs
rules.corrective_language: If the Contractor fails to comply with the Time for Completion, the Contractor shall pay liquidated damages at the rate stated in the Contract Data for every day of delay. The total amount of liquidated damages shall not exceed the maximum stated in the Contract Data. Payment of liquidated damages shall be the Employer's only remedy for the Contractor's failure to complete on time.
rules.financial_exposure: Uncapped LDs on a USD 100M project with USD 150,000 per day LD rate reach the contract value in under 2 years of delay. Uncapped LD exposure drives contractor insolvency and project abandonment — the worst outcome for both parties.

rules.title: Labour & Workforce Compliance
rules.employer_focus: Verify Contractor compliance obligations for labour law, working hours, accommodation standards, and GCC Saudization or Emiratization requirements where applicable.
rules.contractor_focus: Verify Employer-imposed labour requirements are achievable and any additional compliance costs are recoverable as a Variation.
compliance_indicators: Local content or nationalisation requirements stated if applicable
red_flags_employer: No labour compliance obligation on Contractor
GCC regulatory requirements not referenced
red_flags_contractor: Employer-imposed labour standards exceeding statutory requirements without compensation
Saudization or Emiratization targets that are commercially unachievable
rules.corrective_language: The Contractor shall comply with all applicable labour laws including working hour restrictions, minimum wage requirements, accommodation standards, and health and safety regulations. Where applicable, the Contractor shall meet local content requirements as specified in the Contract Data. Any change in statutory requirements after the Base Date shall entitle the Contractor to a Variation.
rules.financial_exposure: Labour compliance failures on GCC projects attract regulatory fines, stop-work orders, and reputational damage. Saudization non-compliance fines under the Nitaqat system can reach SAR 10,000 per worker per month.

rules.title: Materials & Quality Standards
rules.employer_focus: Verify material standards are specified by reference to recognised standards, testing obligations are defined, and Contractor bears cost of rejected materials.
rules.contractor_focus: Verify material standards are achievable in GCC market, testing regime is proportionate, and Engineer approval cannot be unreasonably withheld.
compliance_indicators: Material standards specified by reference to recognised standards
Contractor obligation for rejected materials stated
Engineer inspection rights without hindrance confirmed
Samples and shop drawings submission process defined
red_flags_employer: Material standards defined subjectively without reference to recognised standards
No testing regime allowing disputes over quality
red_flags_contractor: Material standards reference unavailable specifications
Testing regime disproportionate to contract value
Engineer approval withholding rights with no timeline
rules.corrective_language: Plant and Materials shall be of the quality described in the Specification and shall be new unless the Contract otherwise specifies. The Contractor shall submit samples as required. The Engineer shall inspect and test Plant and Materials at the place of manufacture or on Site. The Contractor shall provide all assistance required for inspection.
rules.financial_exposure: Subjective material standards create disputes at every inspection stage. Rejected materials and rework costs on GCC hospitality and infrastructure projects have reached 3-8% of contract value in documented cases.

rules.title: Governing Law & Dispute Seat
rules.employer_focus: Verify governing law is specified, arbitration seat is commercially practical, arbitration institution and rules are stated, and language of arbitration is defined.
rules.contractor_focus: Verify governing law is neutral or familiar, arbitration seat is accessible, and arbitration institution has international enforcement capability.
compliance_indicators: Language of arbitration and Contract stated
red_flags_employer: Governing law conflicts with FIDIC framework principles
Arbitration seat in jurisdiction unfavourable to enforcement
red_flags_contractor: Governing law of Employer country only without neutral option
Arbitration seat inaccessible or unfamiliar to Contractor
No arbitration clause defaulting to local courts only
rules.corrective_language: This Contract shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of [jurisdiction]. Any dispute not resolved by the DAAB shall be finally settled by arbitration under the Rules of the [ICC/DIAC/LCIA]. The seat of arbitration shall be [Dubai/London/Paris]. The language of arbitration shall be English.
rules.financial_exposure: An unfavourable governing law or arbitration seat can make an award unenforceable. In GCC cross-border projects, enforcement of an arbitral award in an unfamiliar jurisdiction can add 2-5 years and hundreds of thousands in legal fees beyond the arbitration itself.
